status: draft; no corpus build, tokenizer training, GPU training, promotion, or deployment is authorized by this file
rationale: Ember v0.0.31 copies 43/90 held-out literals but grounds 0/36 semantic-v1 cases. Tested fine-tuning trajectories showed a learning/preservation trade-off; the separate 0.05 punctuation-weight proposal has not completed a full trajectory.

The base was pretrained on 15,005,553 tokens for a 27,662,848-parameter model (0.54 tokens per parameter, validation loss 4.33). Learning copying and tool routing together on more data is a hypothesis to test, not proof that fine-tuning cannot work.

v0.1.0 proposes a 300M-token corpus (10.8 tokens per parameter per epoch; two epochs reach the ~20 tokens-per-parameter band), with synthetic envelope-copy examples present from step 0. Building the corpus does not establish improved model behavior.

model_reference.architecture_change: none; the same 27.66M EmberGPT is re-pretrained so INT4 export, generate paths, and CPU gates remain valid

tokenizer.seed_policy: balanced by mix share; the envelope_copy slice must be present in the seed sample so JSON scaffolding such as {"arguments":{" and "},"name":" is segmented consistently

general_english.terms_note: Also subject to Common Crawl Terms of Use.
general_english.capacity_note: sample-10BT holds roughly 10B tokens; 120M is well inside the streamed prefix

instruction_following.filter: multi-turn messages rows; exclude source=apigen-80k so tool calling is learned only from Ember-formatted envelopes; render with render_openai_messages
instruction_following.loader: new; OpenAI-style messages column, no tool_calls
instruction_following.synthetic_note: SmolTalk is model-generated instruction data released for small-model pretraining/SFT. It replaces OASST1 as the scalable instruction source because OASST1 is finite at roughly 3M usable English tokens.

instruction_following_human.filter: English, non-deleted assistant replies with their parent prompt
instruction_following_human.capacity_note: 3M tokens is the same absolute demand v0.0.7 met with the headroom-shortfall rule

function_calling.capacity_note: 112,960 rows; 18M + 9M tokens across both Glaive categories is about 40% of the source, so the finite-source shortfall rule must apply to both categories

tool_result_interpretation.filter: real function response followed by assistant interpretation

agent_trajectories.filter: resolved trajectories from permissively licensed repositories

error_recovery.filter: resolved trajectory with a real error result followed by another tool attempt

envelope_copy.license: synthetic; generated deterministically by this repository from no external data
envelope_copy.loader: new; call iter_documents(config) and feed CorpusDocument rows with category envelope_copy
envelope_copy.dedup_note: Documents share templates by design; MinHash near-dedup on five-word shingles at 0.90 would reject valid rows that differ only in the copied value. Exact-hash dedup still applies.
envelope_copy.candidate_note: About 110 tokens per document at 4.8 chars/token, so 180k documents give roughly 20M candidate tokens for the 15M-token share (1.3x headroom, matching candidate_headroom)

sources: config/ember_semantic_v1.json argument_variants and quoted prompt literals
jobs/ember_sft_data_v026.py HELD_OUT_VALUES (90-case copy battery plus corrupted twins)

builder_requirements: Add a smoltalk loader (messages column, OpenAI roles) for instruction_following and keep the OASST1 loader for instruction_following_human.
Add an envelope_copy loader that imports jobs/ember_corpus_envelope_copy_v010.py, streams iter_documents, and skips MinHash near-dedup for that category only.
Apply the finite-source shortfall rule (hard minimum 1.0x, preferred 1.3x) to every source marked finite_source, not only OASST1.

Render assistant turns that contain only a tool call as <|assistant|>\n<|tool|>\n{...} with no empty content line, matching the semantic-v1 prompts; v0.0.7's render_agent_record emits an extra blank line.

Selection and split must stream per category to disk instead of holding every candidate string in memory: 300M tokens is roughly 1.9 GB of candidate text before headroom, above what the 7 GiB GitHub runner can hold alongside the MinHash index.
Write corpus_stats.json with category_selected_tokens for all nine categories and an envelope_copy_audit block copied from the generator's audit output.
hardware_note: Build on a CPU job with at least 16 GiB RAM and 20 GB scratch (HF Jobs cpu-upgrade or a self-hosted runner). The build never launches GPU training.
